scope: Independent read-only source and fixture review; no tests, requests, service, browser or source changes.

files.readScope: Full file: official authorization delegation; media type and byte limit; all stream callbacks and listener cleanup; fail-closed exact Premium source transformation.
Full file: vendored-schema extraction, allowlisted vm module loader, loopback HTTP fixture and cleanup, all five test bodies and their assertions.

conclusions: Official connection.requestRejection is invoked before settings lookup or body handler; unavailable connection returns 503 and explicit rejections never proceed to reads/writes.

JSON media type is normalized and restricted to application/json; complete JSON must be a non-null, non-array object. Byte count includes UTF-8 Buffer lengths, accepts 65536 and rejects greater sizes before parsing or mutation.

Overflow clears buffered chunks and retains a flowing data listener that discards later chunks. end/error/close remove listeners; aborted resolves failure and subsequent close removes listeners. The settled flag prevents a second parse/resolve or a second error response.

Premium replacement anchors are exact-one and ordering is checked; helper import specifier is JSON string escaped. Fixed upstream identity is enforced by its builder, rather than supplied by an HTTP client.

Fixtures open only an ephemeral 127.0.0.1 HTTP server, use in-memory settings, controlled module resolution and synthetic session marker, and destroy their own sockets/server. They do not install packages, access real user profiles or contact external services.
The real 75-case official-server run independently verifies actual 303/cookie session and authorization responses; it is kept separate from the controlled stub guard used by unit fixtures.
coverageLimits: The keep-alive-named fixture proves a successful GET after overflow using one keep-alive agent; it does not assert reuse of the identical TCP socket, so connection-identity preservation is not separately certified.
Premature aborted/error/close behavior is source-reviewed, not covered by an explicit interruption fixture in these five tests. No such test was run or inferred here.

The positive fixture uses one synthetic choice per generic group plus one Premium custom palette, not every real shipped choice. Actual full-choice visual/restart work belongs to the separate root lifecycle verification.
The fixture guard implements the service response contract; it does not implement or validate official cookie cryptography. Official real-runtime evidence covers that exchange separately.
